sentences.text: THESE WRIT PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY
ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) Learned Additional Government Advocate is directed to take notice for the respondents.

2. The petitioners in all these Writ Petitions have called into question the order dated 01.08.2025 passed by the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal, Kalaburagi (for short, 'the Tribunal') in Application Nos.20485/2025, 20482/2025 and 20481/2025, whereby the applications filed by the petitioners for grant of interim orders have been turned down.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6747-DB HC-KAR 3.
The case of the petitioners is that petitioners are working as Food Safety Officers in the Commissionerate of Food Safety at various places.
Initially, they were the employees of Health and Family Welfare Department.
They were working as Food Safety Officers since 2011 in pursuance to the Notification dated 30.07.2011 and Notification dated 05.08.2011.

Vide Government Order dated 23.07.2025 and Official Memorandum dated 25.07.2025, the petitioners were relieved as Food Safety Officers and are directed to report to duty at the office of Commissioner Health and Family Welfare Service as Junior/Senior Health Inspectors and to seek further postings.
4. The petitioners in all these petitions have sought for interim order staying the Government Order dated 23.07.2025 and Official Memorandum dated 25.07.2025.

The Tribunal has refused to grant Shankaragowda S Kanthalagavi vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129618510/
5 exparte interim order.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6747-DB HC-KAR 5.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that similarly placed employees have approached the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal, Bengaluru in Application Nos.3561-3579/2025, wherein the Tribunal has refused to grant interim order.

The same has been called into question before the Principal Bench of this Court at Bengaluru in W.P.No.24182/2025,
whereby this Court vide order dated 19.08.2025 disposed of the Writ Petitions directing the respondents therein to continue the petitioners as Food Safety Officers in the Commissionerate of Food Safety at the place where the petitioners are working for the present till the disposal of that Application.
6.
The order dated 19.08.2025 passed by the Division Bench of this Court is not disputed by the learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondent-State.
7. Since the petitioners in these cases also similarly placed, to maintain parity, the writ petitions are disposed of on similar terms as in W.P.No.24182/2025.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6747-DB HC-KAR 8.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that as on today, the petitioners have not been relieved from their posts.

In case they are not relieved, the respondents are directed to continue the petitioners as Food Safety Officers in the Commissionerate of Food and Safety, at the place where the petitioners are working for the present till disposal of the applications.
9. We request the Tribunal to dispose of the applications as early as possible, as the counsel appearing for the parties have assured that they would co-operate in disposal of the applications.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-
(TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY) JUDGE VNR Shankaragowda S Kanthalagavi vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129618510/
